title: Impact of Obesity Diagnosis on Medication Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use a Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) to estimate the causal impact of receiving an obesity diagnosis on medication use. The key assumption for RDD is that there is a sharp change in the probability of treatment at the cutoff point, and that the running variable (BMI in this case) is as good as randomly assigned around the cutoff. This assumption is often referred to as the "sharp" RDD assumption.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(rdrobust)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s100_data.csv")

# Define the cutoff point for obesity diagnosis
cutoff <- 0.5

# Estimate the RDD model
# We will use the rdrobust package to estimate the RDD model
# The model will estimate the discontinuity in the outcome variable (log medication use) at the cutoff point
result <- rdrobust(data$running_var, data$y, data$treated, c=cutoff, h=0.05)

# Print the estimated discontinuity at the cutoff point
print(result$beta1)

# Basic robustness check: change the bandwidth and check if the results are consistent
result2 <- rdrobust(data$running_var, data$y, data$treated, c=cutoff, h=0.1)
print(result2$beta1)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect a positive coefficient for the discontinuity at the obesity cutoff, indicating that receiving an obesity diagnosis leads to an increase in medication use. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the data, but we expect it to be relatively small since the sample size is relatively small (400 individuals). The reason for expecting a positive effect is that individuals diagnosed with obesity may be more likely to be prescribed medications to manage their condition, such as weight loss medications or medications to manage obesity-related comorbidities.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare medication use for individuals just above and below the BMI cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Receiving an obesity diagnosis at the BMI cutoff leads to increased medication use.
